unit_attributes.statement: In order to promote the establishment and maintenance of a national system of public employment service offices, the United States Employment Service must be established and maintained within the Department of Labor.
unit_attributes.scope_text: In order to promote the establishment and maintenance of a national system of public employment service offices

unit_attributes.statement: For purposes of chapter 4B of title 29, the terms “chief elected official”, “institution of higher education”, “one-stop center”, “one-stop partner”, “training services”, “workforce development activity”, and “workplace learning advisor” have the meaning given the terms in section 3102 of title 29.
For purposes of chapter 4B of title 29, the term “local workforce development board” means a local workforce development board established under section 3122 of title 29.
For purposes of chapter 4B of title 29, the term “one-stop delivery system” means a one-stop delivery system described in section 3151(e) of title 29.
For purposes of chapter 4B of title 29, the term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Labor.
For purposes of chapter 4B of title 29, the term “State” means any of the several States, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Virgin Islands.
For purposes of chapter 4B of title 29, the term “employment service office” means a local office of a State agency.

For purposes of chapter 4B of title 29, except in section 49l–2 of title 29, the term “State agency”, used without further description, means an agency designated or authorized under section 49c of title 29.
unit_attributes.scope_text: For purposes of this chapter, except in section 49l–2 of this title

unit_attributes.statement: The Secretary must assist in coordinating the State public employment service offices throughout the country and in increasing their usefulness by developing and prescribing minimum standards of efficiency, assisting them in meeting problems peculiar to their localities, promoting uniformity in their administrative and statistical procedure, furnishing and publishing information as to opportunities for employment and other information of value in the operation of the system, and maintaining a system for clearing labor between the States.

The Secretary has a duty to assure that unemployment insurance and employment service offices in each State, as appropriate, upon request of a public agency administering or supervising the administration of a State program funded under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act, of a public agency charged with any duty or responsibility under any program or activity authorized or required under part D of title IV of such Act, or of a State agency charged with the administration of the supplemental nutrition assistance program in a State under the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, furnish to such requesting agency, from data contained in their files, specified information regarding any individual specified in the request as to: (1) whether the individual is receiving, has received, or has applied for unemployment compensation, and the amount received; (2) the individual's current (or most recent) home address; and (3) whether the individual has refused an offer of employment and, if so, a description of the employment offered and the terms, conditions, and rate of pay.
unit_attributes.scope_text: upon request of a public agency administering or supervising the administration of a State program funded under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act [42 U.S.C. 601 et seq.], of a public agency charged with any duty or responsibility under any program or activity authorized or required under part D of title IV of such Act [42 U.S.C. 651 et seq.], or of a State agency charged with the administration of the supplemental nutrition assistance program in a State under the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 2011 et seq.)

unit_attributes.statement: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, unemployment insurance and employment service offices in each State, as appropriate, are authorized to furnish to a requesting qualifying agency—namely, a public agency administering or supervising the administration of a State program funded under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act, a public agency charged with any duty or responsibility under any program or activity authorized or required under part D of title IV of such Act, or a State agency charged with administering the supplemental nutrition assistance program under the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008—information from file data regarding an individual specified in the request as to whether the individual receives, received, or applied for unemployment compensation (and the amount), current or most recent home address, and whether the individual refused an offer of employment, with a description of the offered employment and its terms, conditions, and pay rate.
unit_attributes.actor: unemployment insurance and employment service offices in each State
unit_attributes.actor_quote: unemployment insurance and employment service offices in each State
unit_attributes.scope_text: upon request of a public agency administering or supervising the administration of a State program funded under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act [42 U.S.C. 601 et seq.], of a public agency charged with any duty or responsibility under any program or activity authorized or required under part D of title IV of such Act [42 U.S.C. 651 et seq.], or of a State agency charged with the administration of the supplemental nutrition assistance program in a State under the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 2011 et seq.)

unit_attributes.statement: The Secretary must assist in the coordination and development of a nationwide system of public labor exchange services, provided as part of the one-stop customer service systems of the States.

The Secretary must assist in the development of continuous improvement models for the nationwide system of public labor exchange services that ensure private sector satisfaction with the system and meet the demands of jobseekers relating to the system, and must identify and disseminate information on best practices for such system.

The Secretary must ensure, for individuals otherwise eligible to receive unemployment compensation, the provision of reemployment services and other activities in which the individuals are required to participate to receive the compensation.
unit_attributes.scope_text: for individuals otherwise eligible to receive unemployment compensation

unit_attributes.statement: The Secretary must, in coordination with the State agencies and the staff of such agencies, assist in the planning and implementation of activities to enhance the professional development and career advancement opportunities of such staff, in order to strengthen the provision of a broad range of career guidance services, the identification of job openings (including providing intensive outreach to small and medium-sized employers and enhanced employer services), the provision of technical assistance and training to other providers of workforce development activities (including workplace learning advisors) relating to counseling and employment-related services, and the development of new strategies for coordinating counseling and technology.

In order to improve service delivery, avoid duplication of services, and enhance coordination of services, including location of staff to ensure access to services under section 49f(a) of title 29 statewide in underserved areas, employment service offices in each State must be colocated with one-stop centers.

The Secretary, in consultation with States, is authorized to assist the States in the development of national electronic tools that may be used to improve access to workforce information for individuals through the one-stop delivery systems established as described in section 3151(e) of title 29, and through such other delivery systems as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.
